title: What a Statute of Frauds does and does not do
shortTitle: What a Statute of Frauds does and does not do
summary: The statute’s enforcement barrier is distinct from the existence and other consequences of an agreement.
notes: The chapter separates formation, statutory coverage, compliant evidence, and exceptions. A defense may be waived; a signature may bind one party without the same evidence against the other. The agreement can have consequences for restitution, property, defenses, or interference even when an action to enforce it is barred. The precise consequence depends on the claim and the provision, not the word “void” used loosely.
